name: Rear Brake Pads
summary: Rear pad job on a floating caliper with a separate mechanical drum-in-hat parking brake (3 sources), so no electronic-parking-brake service mode. Second pass settled the tool confusion: the 16 mm (5/8 in) bolts that bmwtuning, DriveDIY and Pelican tell you to remove are the CARRIER bolts (65 Nm per Autodoc and BMW-data table), while the caliper itself is held by two guide screws (13 mm hexagon head at 35 Nm per Autodoc; BMW-data table also lists a 30 Nm socket-head variant). The rear wear sensor is on the passenger (right) rear only (3 sources). Rear pad 34216774692 and its newer interchange 34216790761 are verified by two sites; rotors are 300x20 (RWD 34216764651, xDrive 34216764653). Rear guide-screw torque is only single-sourced (Autodoc) and rear rotor minimum thickness is unresolved, so verify on the car. No BMW primary document was reachable.
variantDependencies: VIN WBAPH7C58AA175760 decodes at NHTSA vPIC to BMW 328i, 2010, Sedan, 3.0 L, 230 hp, Munich, TPMS Direct (check digit valid). Engine code N52B30 is consistent but not stated by NHTSA. [https://vpic.nhtsa.dot.gov/api/vehicles/DecodeVinValues/WBAPH7C58AA175760?format=json&modelyear=2010]

RWD vs xDrive: NHTSA returns AWD for sister pattern WBAPK7C5 and no drive type for this VIN's WBAPH7C5, suggesting RWD; owner should confirm. Affects rotor PN (RWD 34216764651, xDrive 34216764653) and pad listings (Jurid lists 328i xDrive 2009-2012).

Production date: model year 2010 only. Rear sensor splits at 03/2010 (789445 up to, 792564 from). Rear pad 34216774692 is listed 2006-2009 by Turner, 2007-2010 by PMB; Alleuro/Turner cross-reference it to 34216790761 (Jurid 2009-2012 xDrive).
Brake package: the Jurid listing warns multiple brake package options exist and asks for VIN; rear rotor is 300x20 per Turner for 328i and 328xi.

Rear caliper guide hardware: Autodoc rear guide uses hexagon-head screws (13 mm socket, 15 mm back-up wrench, 35 Nm). A BMW-data table also lists a socket-head variant (30 Nm). Inspect the head type on the car.
Engine and transmission: no source shows any effect on this job.

tools.item: Jack, rated jack stands, wheel chocks (chock the front wheels)
17 mm wheel-bolt socket and breaker bar

tools.conflicts: Earlier ledger recorded Team-BHP '17 mm hex' as a guide-bolt size; no other site agrees. The 16 mm / 5/8 in tool is consistently attached to the carrier ('caliper') bolts.

tools.item: 13 mm socket plus 15 mm open-end back-up wrench for the rear guide screws (Autodoc rear guide); hex head type must be confirmed on the car
tools.conflicts: Only Autodoc lists 13/15 mm; Bolidenforum BMW-data lists both hexagon and socket-head guide-screw variants without sizes.

tools.item: Piston reset: spreader, C-clamp or wind-back tool (plain push-back; no rotate tool required per the sources found)
10 mm socket for the wheel-arch cover fasteners to reach the sensor plug
Brake cleaner, copper grease for wheel-to-hub face, caliper grease for guide pins, anti-squeal paste
No EPB service-mode tool needed (mechanical handbrake)

steps.title: Prepare and chock
steps.instruction: Chock the front wheels, open the hood and unscrew the brake-fluid reservoir cap (optional; keeps the level from overfilling). Leave the parking brake released for the whole job. Do not press the pedal while the caliper is off.
warnings: Release the parking brake before removing a rotor; the youcanic guide says leaving it applied can damage the shoes, and Pelican staff also advise leaving it off.
Chock the front wheels.

steps.title: Loosen wheel bolts, lift and support the rear
steps.instruction: Break the 17 mm wheel bolts loose on the ground, then lift the rear and place rated stands. Do not lift on the aluminium differential cover. Forum sources conflict about the rear centre point (cast-iron differential housing vs crossmember vs not permitted), so use the side jack points (plastic pads at the sills) with stands.
warnings: Never work under a car on a jack alone.
Do not rely on the parking brake to hold a car on stands.

steps.title: Remove the wheel
steps.instruction: Remove the bolts and the wheel.
warnings: Support the wheel.

steps.title: Remove the anti-rattle clip
steps.instruction: Pull or pry the retaining clip off the front of the caliper by hand or with a screwdriver.
warnings: Wear eye protection.

steps.title: Passenger side only: free the wear sensor
steps.instruction: Only the right (passenger) rear pad has a sensor. Pull it from the pad with a flat screwdriver, remove the 10 mm fasteners on the wheel-arch cover (or partly lower the liner), unplug the connector at the black box and unclip the wire. Skip on the driver side.
warnings: Sensors are brittle; always replace.
Driver-side rear has no sensor.

steps.title: Release the caliper (choose method)
steps.instruction: Method A (guide screws): clean the screws with a wire brush, hold the pin flat with a 15 mm wrench if hexagon-head and loosen the two screws with a 13 mm socket, remove them and lift the caliper off the carrier. Method B (carrier bolts, used in the bmwtuning/DriveDIY guides): remove the two 16 mm (5/8 in) bolts from behind and lift the caliper and carrier off together. Support the caliper without loading the hose.
warnings: Identify the screw head type first.
Never hang the caliper by the hose.
Carrier bolt re-torque 65 Nm if Method B.

steps.title: Remove the pads and clips
steps.instruction: Slide out the outer pad; the inner pad is held by a clip in the piston and pries out. Remove the pad retaining clips from the carrier with a screwdriver and clean the carrier with a wire brush and brake cleaner.

steps.title: Inspect rotor and parking-brake area
steps.instruction: Measure rotor thickness against the MIN TH stamp (rear rotor is 300 x 20 new). The handbrake shoes sit inside the rotor hat, not in the caliper; if the rotor was pulled, the parking brake needs readjusting afterwards.
warnings: Published minimums conflict; the stamp governs.
Rotor replacement requires parking-brake readjustment (Pelican staff).

steps.title: Clean, lubricate and refit clips
steps.instruction: Fit new retaining clips if supplied, put silicone-based grease on guide-pin sliding surfaces (not mineral oil near rubber), a thin film of anti-squeal paste on pad contact points, and check pin boots.
warnings: Keep grease off friction surfaces.

steps.title: Retract the piston
steps.instruction: Push the piston straight back with a spreader or clamp against the old pad, watching the reservoir. The parking brake is not inside the caliper, so no rotation is needed per the sources.
warnings: Check reservoir level.

steps.title: Fit new pads and sensor
steps.instruction: Install new pads (friction faces toward rotor), press the new sensor into the passenger-side rear inner pad channel and route the wire as before.
warnings: Wrong-length sensor was fitted first by the Team-BHP author; compare length with the old one.

steps.title: Refit the caliper and torque
steps.instruction: Method A: refit and torque the two guide screws (35 Nm for hexagon-head per Autodoc; 30 Nm for a socket-head per BMW-data table; both single-sourced). Method B: carrier bolts to 65 Nm, caliper then refitted as above. Refit the clip, dust caps and sensor plug and cover.
warnings: Guide-screw torque is single-sourced; carrier torque is secondary (Autodoc plus BMW-data).

steps.title: Wheel on and torque
steps.instruction: Clean the hub face, mount the wheel, start bolts by hand, lower the car and torque to 120 Nm in a crisscross sequence.
warnings: Torque is secondary-sourced; BMW TIS (per Department 69) says to re-check after installation.

steps.title: Pump pedal, check fluid
steps.instruction: Pump the pedal until firm before starting the engine, then top up to MAX with DOT 4 low-viscosity fluid.
warnings: Do not drive until the pedal is firm.

steps.title: Test the parking brake and bed in
steps.instruction: With the car chocked, check the handbrake holds; road-test at low speed and avoid hard braking for about 150 to 200 km.
warnings: If the lever travel is long after a rotor swap, adjust the shoes (see Pelican's parking brake article).

steps.title: Reset the rear brake service item
steps.instruction: Ignition on, use the trip button to reach the rear brake service item and reset; scan tool fallback. A new rear sensor must be fitted and both axle sensors intact.
warnings: Some readers report 2010 clusters refusing a manual reset.

safety: Rated jack stands only; do not jack on the differential cover.
Parking brake is a mechanical drum-in-hat; do not rely on it as the only restraint and release it before pulling a rotor.
Chock front wheels; do not let the caliper hang from the hose.
Keep grease off friction surfaces and rotor.
Torque values here are secondary-sourced; guide-screw torque is single-sourced.
Pump the pedal to firm before moving the car and test at low speed.
missingEvidence: No BMW primary document (TIS, Bentley, owner's manual) was reachable.
A second independent source for rear guide-screw torque (35 Nm hexagon / 30 Nm socket-head) and for rear guide-screw tool sizes.
Rear rotor minimum thickness: Pelican's 22.4 mm 'rear' value is impossible for a 20 mm new rotor and another Pelican article is inconsistent; read the MIN TH stamp.
Rear sensor 34356792564 fitment for a 328i built after 03/2010 beyond Turner listings.
Parking-brake shoe adjustment procedure details (Pelican has a separate article, not fetched).
Whether xDrive changes any rear hardware beyond rotor/pad part numbers.
ownerInputsNeeded: RWD vs xDrive confirmation (rotor PN, pad listing).
Rear guide-screw head type (hexagon vs socket-head) and the rotor MIN TH stamp.
Whether the passenger-side rear sensor is currently plugged in and its length.

visuals.title: Rear caliper: clip, guide screws and carrier bolts

elements.describe: A floating disc-brake caliper on the rear rotor seen from the outboard side with the wheel removed.
A spring clip on the front of the caliper that comes off by hand or with a screwdriver.
Two hex-head bolts (16 mm) on the back side of the caliper carrier.
Two guide screws that hold the caliper to the carrier; head type (hexagon or socket) is not established.

facts.note: 2 sites: clip on the front of the caliper; Autodoc lists retaining clips on the carrier for the pads.
4 sites: 16 mm (5/8 in) bolts; BMW-data table agrees on 65 Nm.
2 sites: two bolts on the back side, one top and one bottom (DriveDIY).
1 site: hexagon 13 mm with 15 mm back-up flats; other sources unspecified.
Pages describe the rear caliper on the rotor with its bracket bolted behind it; no richer placement statement exists.
BMWTuning: clip protrudes from the front of the caliper; Autodoc: retaining clips removed with flat screwdriver; DriveDIY: clip to come out.
Pelican and DriveDIY: 16mm rear bracket bolts (18mm front); BMWTuning: two bolts on the back side of the caliper (5/8 socket).
Pelican: reached behind the caliper; DriveDIY: inner side of the caliper; BMWTuning: back side of the caliper.

mustNotDepict.reason: Head type and exact position are only single-sourced.
Exact shape and engagement not established.

3 sites: arch cover or fender liner (10 mm fasteners per Autodoc) hides the plug in a black box.
1 site: connector release tab; shape not described.
